title: Perfume Discovery Set Pack-Out: Keep Scent Names and Vials Matched
seoTitle: Perfume Discovery Set Pack-Out Checklist | MTT
summary: Plan vial identification, insert positions and card revisions before a fragrance discovery set is packed.
intro: We start a perfume discovery set by laying the filled vials beside the scent card. If two labels look alike, the person packing the set needs a reliable way to match each vial to its position, and the customer needs to identify it after removal. Agree the identification system, physical layout and pack-out checks before approving the final box and artwork.
cta: Send your vial list, capped dimensions, scent names, card artwork, quantity by design and packing location. MTT can review the packaging brief for projects from 1,000 boxes per design.
sections: Separate the three pieces of information

A set can carry a fragrance name on the vial, beside its cavity and on a separate scent card. Decide what the customer sees while the vial is in the tray and what remains identifiable after it is removed. A number on the tray cannot identify an unmarked vial once several vials are outside the box.

We would ask the brand to approve one master list linking each scent name, item code, tray position and card description. The six-channel double-door box is a design reference for discussing positions, not evidence of a particular customer packing operation.
Give the packer a position map

Define a fixed orientation: for example, doors open toward the operator and position 1 begins at the left. Number the drawing in the same direction as the physical tray. Document which vials, insert and card belong to each set version; a visual colour cue can help but should not be the only identification method when colours or lighting are similar.

Illustrative scenario: a six-vial collection is offered in two combinations that share four scents. The outer boxes look identical but the last two positions and cards differ. Keep separate packing maps and version identifiers; trial each combination before approving production. This is an example, not an MTT customer order.
Test readability on the actual assembled set

Sample-stage identification checks
Point in useQuestion to answerRecord
Before loadingCan the packer distinguish similar vials and version labels?Approved component list
In the trayAre names or position numbers visible without turning the vial?Loaded sample photo and orientation
After removalCan each vial still be identified and returned?Label and card revision
At dispatchDoes the outer identifier match the set inside?Version and pack-out record

If barcode or QR identification is part of the agreed system, test the printed symbol on the finished material in the actual position. GS1 notes that contrast, quiet zones, surface curvature and sheen can affect scanning.[1] A successful phone scan alone is not a formal barcode verification grade.
Check fit without hiding the identification

The vial, label and cap must be represented in the structural sample. A tight opening can conceal a name or rub a label when a vial is removed. Check access to each vial without relying on the cap as the only grip, and keep the card from pressing on closures when the lid shuts. Compare the initial layout in the discovery set design guide.
Ask for a comparable production brief

State who supplies and fills the vials, who applies labels and who packs the set. Quote the box, insert, card, version changes, sampling and shipping separately. A shared outer box may still require separate inserts or cards. Confirm the exact component revisions and quantities for each design, starting at 1,000 boxes per design. Review discovery set box formats before selecting the opening.
Sources
1. GS1: 2D barcodes in retail, print and placement considerations, accessed 16 November 2026.

title: Magnetic Gift Box Lid Not Closing Flush? A Sample Troubleshooting Guide
seoTitle: Magnetic Box Lid Not Closing: Sample Checks | MTT
summary: Diagnose a magnetic rigid box lid that lifts, catches or closes unevenly using the finished loaded sample.
intro: We close the magnetic gift box with the intended insert and filled products in place. If the lid stands proud or one corner lifts, we first look for physical interference and alignment before changing the magnets. Compare the empty and loaded sample, inspect the hinge and wrapped surfaces, and record the configuration so the converter can investigate the right cause.
cta: Send the box drawing, filled product dimensions, insert layout, closure photos and quantity per design. MTT can review a magnetic-box sample brief for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: First separate loaded interference from shell geometry

Close the empty shell on a flat surface, then add the insert, product and card one at a time. Note when the lid changes position. A tall pump, raised insert edge or folded leaflet can touch the lid before the closure faces meet. If the empty shell also sits unevenly, inspect hinge movement, panel shape and the wrapped edges. Do not press a sample flat and treat that as approval.

The skincare book-style box shows a hinged presentation layout. It is a design reference, not evidence that any other product fits or that its closure has been tested.
Read the symptom without assuming a single cause

What to compare on the finished sample
ObservationInvestigateNext comparison
Only loaded box liftsProduct or insert contact with lidAdd components one at a time
One corner lifts when emptyHinge, panel, wrap or closure positionCompare a second finished sample
Lid shifts sidewaysClosure alignment and hinge positionMark positions on approved drawing
Closure weak through finishMagnet pairing, intervening layers and geometryCompare complete finished constructions

These are investigation routes, not proof of a root cause. Humidity, materials and production variation also need project-specific review.
Why the finished material stack matters

Magnet performance depends on the actual pairing and separation. The magnet supplier Supermagnete explains that attractive force drops as separation increases and that surface conditions matter.[1] In a wrapped box, the board recess, cover, lining and alignment all form part of the finished construction to review. Its published measurements are not specifications or test results for an MTT box.

Ask the converter to identify the closure arrangement and drawing revision. Compare alternatives on finished samples with the same wrap, insert and contents; a stronger magnet can change opening feel and does not fix a product physically pushing the lid away.
Make acceptance observable

Agree which orientation, contents and surface are used when checking closure. Record edge alignment, visible lifting, opening and closing feel, and any movement after normal handling. Ask the responsible parties to define a project-specific method and acceptance range; there is no universal lid gap or magnet force stated here. Compare several representative samples where feasible and keep any measurements with their sample IDs.

Illustrative example: if an empty sample closes normally but lifts only when a serum with its dropper is installed, measure the complete closed product and lid clearance before changing the magnets. This is an engineering example, not a reported customer defect.
Confirm the complete delivery scope

Provide the filled products, artwork and insert revision, quantity per design and destination. Ask what is included in shell, insert, magnet, sampling and tooling charges. If the box will be shipped as a filled set, agree the outer packaging and distribution test separately: a magnetic snap is not a shipping certification. See the book-style construction guide and change and retest checklist.
Sources
1. Supermagnete: factors affecting magnetic holding force, accessed 16 November 2026.
